_comment: Curated content for the eight flagship project pages. Structured facts (dates, contract form, appointment, band, employer) are read from tools/projects.json by name, so they cannot drift from the database; everything else is written here. Privacy rules of the public repo apply: no monetary values (bands only), no contact names, phone numbers or email addresses, nothing from disputes, legal or financial-account material. Brands are listed only where the project database or a project document evidences them. Representative photographs are labelled as such. Then run: python3 tools/project_pages.py build

thabazimbi-10ml-dome-roof-reservoir.title: Thabazimbi 10ML Dome Roof Reservoir | Unicon
thabazimbi-10ml-dome-roof-reservoir.description: 10 ML post-tensioned concrete reservoir with a column-free dome roof at Thabazimbi, Limpopo, built by Unicon under a GCC 2010 full contract.
thabazimbi-10ml-dome-roof-reservoir.lead: A 10 megalitre reinforced concrete reservoir with post-tensioned walls and a free-spanning dome roof, built by Unicon at Thabazimbi, Limpopo.

image.alt: Reinforced concrete dome roof under construction on a circular water reservoir

overview: Thabazimbi is a mining town in the Limpopo bushveld, and water storage there has to be reliable for people and industry alike. Unicon built a 10 ML reinforced concrete reservoir with post-tensioned circular walls and a dome roof that spans the whole tank without a single internal column.

A column-free dome keeps the floor of the tank clear, removes the leak paths that roof columns create and gives a roof that is structurally efficient over a large diameter. It is also among the least forgiving things to build in concrete: the walls are stressed with post-tensioning tendons, the roof is formed and poured as a single geometric shell, and every pour has to be tested, recorded and signed off before the next one starts.

scope.title: Recorded scope
items: 10 ML reinforced concrete reservoir
Post-tensioned concrete walls
Free-spanning dome roof with no column supports
Connecting pipework and chambers

scope.title: Unicon's standard controls on this type of work
items: Concrete cube testing, slump and temperature records for every pour
Watertightness testing of the completed reservoir
As-built records and handover

brands.name: Anglo American
brands.note: Global mining group; the client on this contract.

faq.q: What is a post-tensioned concrete reservoir?
faq.a: The circular wall contains steel tendons that are tensioned after the concrete has gained strength. This pre-compresses the wall so it stays in compression when the stored water pushes outwards, which keeps cracking, and therefore leakage, under control.

faq.q: Why build a dome roof without columns?
faq.a: With no internal columns the roof is a self-supporting shell. The tank floor stays clear, there are fewer penetrations to waterproof, and the structure is efficient over a large span. It does demand precise formwork and disciplined concrete placement.

faq.q: What was Unicon's scope on this reservoir?
faq.a: Unicon built the whole reservoir structure and its connecting pipework and chambers under GCC 2010 (General Conditions of Contract for Construction Works), carrying responsibility for the concrete works, the programme and the quality of its work.

faq.q: Does Unicon build water reservoirs for mines and municipalities?
faq.a: Yes. Reservoirs and bulk water works are the largest part of the Unicon portfolio, with fifty projects in the project database for municipalities, water boards and industrial clients.

tinley-manor-wwtw-club-med.title: Tinley Manor WWTW for Club Med Resort | Unicon
tinley-manor-wwtw-club-med.description: New wastewater treatment works with reedbeds for the Club Med resort development at Tinley Manor, Ballito, built by Unicon under a GCC 2015 full contract.
tinley-manor-wwtw-club-med.lead: A new wastewater treatment works, including reedbeds, built by Unicon as principal contractor to serve the Club Med resort development on the KwaZulu-Natal North Coast.

image.alt: Concrete pour for the reedbed wastewater treatment works at Club Med Tinley Manor, Ballito

overview: A resort of this size needs its own sanitation infrastructure, and it needs it ready before the doors open. Unicon was appointed on a full contract to construct the proposed new wastewater treatment works for the Club Med hotel development at Tinley Manor, near Ballito.

The works combine reinforced concrete process structures with pipework, valves, pumps and steel, and include reedbed treatment cells. The programme was short, about five months, which made early procurement of pumps and valves and tight coordination of concrete pours the critical path.

scope.title: Recorded scope
items: New wastewater treatment works for the Club Med hotel development
Reedbed treatment cells, with concrete pours placed in March 2025
Concrete structures, pipework, valves, pumps and steelwork
Programme of about five months from October 2024

scope.title: Unicon's standard controls on this type of work
items: Concrete cube testing and records for every pour
Watertightness testing of liquid-retaining structures
As-built records and handover

brands.name: Club Med
brands.note: International resort brand; the works serve its hotel development at Tinley Manor.

faq.q: What does a wastewater treatment works for a resort involve?
faq.a: Reinforced concrete treatment structures, interconnecting pipework, pumps and valves, and the treatment process itself. At Tinley Manor this includes reedbeds, which treat effluent biologically in planted, lined cells.

faq.q: What contract form was used?
faq.a: GCC 2015, the General Conditions of Contract for Construction Works, on a full contract. Unicon was the principal contractor and carried programme, quality and subcontractor coordination.

faq.q: Can Unicon build treatment works for private developers as well as municipalities?
faq.a: Yes. Most Unicon wastewater work has been for municipalities and water boards, but the same disciplines apply to private developments, where the works usually have to be ready before the buildings they serve.

howick-on-main-retail-centre.title: Howick on Main Retail Centre Construction | Unicon
howick-on-main-retail-centre.description: 7,600 m² Howick on Main shopping centre with Checkers, Dis-Chem, Ocean Basket, Spur, Mugg & Bean and Mr Price, managed by Unicon under JBCC 6.2.
howick-on-main-retail-centre.lead: A 7,600 m² retail centre with Checkers, Dis-Chem, Ocean Basket, Spur, Mugg & Bean and Mr Price as anchor tenants, delivered by Unicon as construction manager to a design by Visi Architects.

image.alt: Structural steel frame rising over groundworks

overview: Howick on Main is a new 7,600 m² retail centre in the KwaZulu-Natal Midlands. Its anchor tenants are some of South Africa's best-known national brands, and each brings its own fit-out requirements, opening date and landlord obligations.

Unicon was appointed here as construction manager under JBCC Series 6.2, not as a lump-sum main contractor. In that role Unicon's job is to plan the programme, manage the trade contractors, control cost and quality and keep the centre moving towards a fixed trading date. It is the appointment most often used on retail developments where tenant requirements are still evolving while the structure goes up.

scope.title: Recorded scope
items: New retail centre of approximately 7,600 m² with Checkers, Dis-Chem, Mr Price, Ocean Basket, Spur and Mugg & Bean as anchor tenants
Construction in steel, concrete, brick, glass and roofing
Architectural design by Visi Architects
Programme of 17 months from June 2023

scope.title: What a construction management appointment covers
items: Programme planning and tracking across all trades
Appointment, coordination and supervision of trade contractors
Cost control and reporting against the budget
Health, safety and quality management on site

brands.name: Checkers
brands.note: National supermarket brand of the Shoprite Group.

faq.q: What is the difference between a full contract and construction management?
faq.a: On a full contract the contractor holds one agreement with the employer and takes responsibility for delivering the whole building for the agreed price. As construction manager the contractor plans and manages the trade contractors on the employer's behalf, with cost and programme control, which gives the employer more visibility and flexibility while the design is still developing.

faq.q: Which national brands trade at Howick on Main?
faq.a: The anchor tenants are Checkers, Dis-Chem, Mr Price, Ocean Basket, Spur and Mugg & Bean.

faq.q: Does Unicon build shopping centres in KwaZulu-Natal?
faq.a: Yes. Unicon has delivered retail centres in Howick and Pietermaritzburg, including the 17,000 m² Invesco centre, as well as education and healthcare buildings.

faq.q: Which JBCC edition was used?
faq.a: JBCC Series 6.2, the current Joint Building Contracts Committee agreement.

mnqumashe-high-throughput-abattoir.title: Mnqumashe High Throughput Abattoir | Unicon
mnqumashe-high-throughput-abattoir.description: High throughput cattle and sheep abattoir near Butterworth, Eastern Cape: demolition, platforms, portal-frame steel and mechanical install. Unicon, JBCC.
mnqumashe-high-throughput-abattoir.lead: A new high throughput cattle and sheep abattoir in the Eastern Cape: demolition of the old building, cut-to-fill platforms, portal-frame steel structures and a full services and mechanical equipment installation.
overview: The Mnqumashe abattoir, in the Mnquma Local Municipality near Butterworth, is a high throughput facility for cattle and sheep. It sits in the R50M+ value band and is among the most complex projects in the Unicon portfolio, because an abattoir is a building and a production line at the same time: floors fall to drains, surfaces are washable, and every service has to land exactly where the equipment needs it.

Unicon carried out the works under JBCC Series 5. The work began with demolition of the existing building and earthworks to form new cut-to-fill platforms, followed by the portal-frame steel structure and the installation of all services and mechanical equipment.

scope.title: Recorded scope
items: Demolition of the existing building
Cut-to-fill earthworks forming new platforms
New facility in portal-frame structural steel
Installation of all services
Installation of the mechanical equipment
Concrete works and pipework

scope.title: Contract and programme
items: JBCC Series 5 full contract, 29 months from October 2017
Quantity surveying by LDM Quantity Surveying
R50M+ value band

brands.name: Department of Rural Development and Land Reform
brands.note: National department; the abattoir is in the Eastern Cape.

brands.name: LDM Quantity Surveying
brands.note: Appointed quantity surveyor on the contract.

faq.q: What makes an abattoir harder to build than a standard industrial building?
faq.a: Hygiene and process drive everything. Floors must fall to drains, surfaces must be impervious and washable, and the building has to be finished around the equipment, which means civil, steel and mechanical trades are tightly coordinated.

faq.q: Did Unicon install the mechanical equipment?
faq.a: Yes. The scope covered all services and the abattoir mechanical equipment.

faq.q: Does Unicon build agricultural and food-processing facilities?
faq.a: Yes. Agricultural EPC includes dairies, abattoirs, packhouses and irrigation infrastructure. Mnqumashe sits alongside food-industry work for Nestlé.

faq.q: What contract form was used?
faq.a: JBCC Series 5, with Unicon carrying out the full scope of the works.

invesco-shopping-mall-pietermaritzburg.title: Invesco Shopping Mall Pietermaritzburg | Unicon
invesco-shopping-mall-pietermaritzburg.description: 17,000 m² three-storey Invesco retail centre in Pietermaritzburg with basement parking. Unicon built all concrete structure works in a JV, JBCC Series 4.
invesco-shopping-mall-pietermaritzburg.lead: A 17,000 m² three-storey retail centre with basement parking, ground-floor shops and first-floor offices and restaurants, delivered in joint venture with Carlos Da Costa Building, with Unicon constructing all the concrete structure.

image.alt: Tower crane and scaffolding over the Invesco Centre construction site, Pietermaritzburg

overview: The Invesco Centre in Pietermaritzburg is a three-storey retail building of roughly 17,000 m². It combines basement parking, ground-floor shop space and first-floor office and restaurant space, a stacked layout that puts the weight of the structure squarely on the concrete frame.

Unicon took the contract in a joint venture with Carlos Da Costa Building and constructed all of the concrete structural works. The programme ran for twenty months, from April 2008, under JBCC Series 4.

scope.title: Recorded scope
items: New three-storey retail centre of approximately 17,000 m²
Basement parking, ground-floor shop space and first-floor office and restaurant space
All concrete structure works, with formwork, steel reinforcement and concrete
Joint venture with Carlos Da Costa Building

scope.title: Contract and programme
items: JBCC Series 4 full contract, 20 months from April 2008
R20-50M value band

brands.name: Carlos Da Costa Building
brands.note: Building contractor in the joint venture with Unicon.

faq.q: What did Unicon build at the Invesco Centre?
faq.a: All of the concrete structure of a three-storey building of about 17,000 m² with basement parking, delivered in joint venture with Carlos Da Costa Building.

faq.q: Does Unicon work in joint venture?
faq.a: Yes, where a project suits it. Joint ventures allow each partner to carry the trades it is strongest in, and Unicon's structural concrete capability is typically what it brings.

faq.q: Can Unicon build basement parking and multi-storey concrete frames?
faq.a: Yes. Basement parking and multi-storey reinforced concrete structure are in the recorded scope at the Invesco Centre, and structural concrete is a core Unicon capability.

faq.q: What contract form was used?
faq.a: JBCC Series 4.

makhathini-drainage-canal-jozini.title: Makhathini Drainage Canal, Jozini | Unicon
makhathini-drainage-canal-jozini.description: 4 km concrete-lined drainage canal for farmland on the Mjindi Plantations near Jozini, KwaZulu-Natal, carried out by Unicon under GCC 2010.
makhathini-drainage-canal-jozini.lead: Excavation and concrete lining of a 4 km drainage canal serving farmland on the Mjindi Plantations near Jozini, carried out by Unicon under GCC 2010.

image.alt: Excavator shaping a canal through red soil

overview: The Makhathini Flats in northern KwaZulu-Natal are fertile farmland that depends on managing water in both directions. Unicon excavated and lined a 4 km concrete drainage canal to carry water off the farmland of the Mjindi Plantations near Jozini.

A concrete canal is a long, thin project, so the work is about repeatability: setting out and excavating to line and level, then placing the lining consistently along the whole length. The contract ran for 24 months from November 2014 under GCC 2010.

scope.title: Recorded scope
items: Excavation of approximately 4 km of canal
Concrete lining of the canal
Drainage of farmland on the Mjindi Plantations near Jozini
Materials: concrete and aggregate

scope.title: Contract and programme
items: GCC 2010 full contract, 24 months from November 2014
R20-50M value band

brands.name: Mjindi Plantations
brands.note: The farmland drained by the canal.

faq.q: How long is the Makhathini drainage canal?
faq.a: The canal Unicon excavated and lined is approximately 4 km long.

faq.q: Why line a drainage canal with concrete?
faq.a: A concrete lining stops erosion and scour, holds the canal's shape and reduces maintenance, especially on flat farmland where water movement is slow and sediment builds up.

faq.q: Does Unicon build canals and large earthworks projects?
faq.a: Yes. Canals, bulk earthworks, bridges and drainage structures sit within Unicon's heavy civils work, much of it for provincial and municipal clients.

faq.q: What contract form was used?
faq.a: GCC 2010, General Conditions of Contract for Construction Works, as a full contract.

nestle-coffee-factory-upgrade.title: Nestlé Coffee Factory Upgrade | Unicon Construction
nestle-coffee-factory-upgrade.description: Upgrades and additions to the Nestlé coffee factory: evaporator building, cooling tower tanks, control rooms and 900 NB stormwater. Unicon, GCC 2004.
nestle-coffee-factory-upgrade.lead: Upgrades and additions to the Nestlé coffee factory: a new evaporator building, extension of the tin can manufacturing room, switch control rooms, cooling tower tanks and large stormwater retention works, delivered by Unicon under GCC 2004.

image.alt: Crane lifting a large industrial vessel into position

overview: Upgrading an existing food factory is a different discipline from building on an empty site. New structures have to tie into old ones, services have to be rerouted, and every demolition has to be planned around what stays.

Unicon was appointed on a full contract under GCC 2004 for upgrades and additions to the Nestlé coffee factory. The 24-month programme, from March 2008, combined demolition, new buildings, process-supporting structures and a substantial civil package for stormwater and retention.

scope.title: Buildings and structures
items: Demolition of existing structures and construction of a new parking lot
New switch control rooms
Extension of the tin can manufacturing room
New evaporator building
Other upgrades, extensions and restorations

scope.title: Tanks and external works
items: New waste storage tanks
Cooling tower tanks
New terraces and external works

scope.title: Pipework and stormwater
items: All associated pipework
900 NB stormwater pipes
Large stormwater retention tanks

scope.title: Contract and programme
items: GCC 2004 full contract, 24 months from March 2008
R20-50M value band

brands.name: Nestlé
brands.note: Global food and beverage company; Unicon has delivered work for Nestlé SA more than once, including milk depot alterations in 2003.

faq.q: Does Unicon carry out upgrades to existing industrial facilities?
faq.a: Yes. The Nestlé coffee factory scope included demolition, extension of existing buildings, restorations and new process buildings, all of which have to tie into what is already there.

faq.q: What was built at the Nestlé coffee factory?
faq.a: An evaporator building, switch control rooms, an extension to the tin can manufacturing room, cooling tower tanks, waste storage tanks, terraces, a new parking lot, large stormwater retention tanks and the associated pipework.

faq.q: What contract form was used?
faq.a: GCC 2004, General Conditions of Contract for Construction Works, as a full contract.

faq.q: Has Unicon worked for Nestlé before?
faq.a: Yes. Unicon also carried out alterations and extensions to the Nestlé milk depot in 2003 and 2004.
